steps.text: Find the insertion position without changing any links, so duplicates or a full pool can fail safely.
Repeat while current differs from -1 and self.data[current] is less than value.
Check whether current differs from -1 and self.data[current] equals value or self.free equals -1.
Detach the first free slot before attaching it to a live list; each slot must have exactly one owner.
Repeat while current differs from -1 and self.data[current] differs from value.
Return the removed slot to the free chain so either list can reuse its capacity.

lesson.approach: Treat each array index as a node. The two live lists and the free chain share the same next array; every slot must belong to exactly one chain. Search first, then change links only when the operation can succeed.

steps.text: Initialise one free chain through all slots. Both live heads are -1 because neither list contains values yet.
Track both the current node and its predecessor. Stop at the insertion point; reject a duplicate or full pool before consuming a slot.
Remove one slot from the free chain and link it before current. Update the list head when there is no predecessor; otherwise update the predecessor’s next link.
Find and unlink the target, then put its slot at the front of the free chain. Recycling makes that capacity available to either list.
Follow links, not physical array order. The returned list is only an output copy; it is not the structure’s storage.

lesson.trace: Pool(2): free is 0 → 1 → -1. insert(0, 7) gives list 0 slot 0, leaving free=1. insert(1, 9) uses slot 1, leaving free=-1. delete(0, 7) returns slot 0 to free. insert(1, 8) reuses slot 0 before slot 1: list 1 now contains [8, 9].
mistakes: Changing next[current] before unlinking the node can lose the rest of its live list.
Allocating before checking duplicates can leak a free slot.
A duplicate is forbidden within one list; the same value is allowed in the other list.
lesson.complexity: For a selected list of n nodes, insert and delete take O(n) in the worst case; relinking a known node takes O(1). values takes O(n). Extra space context: storage is O(capacity); values creates an O(n) output list.
